pageDescription: Clear and consistent date and time formats reduce ambiguity across different regions and make time-sensitive data easy to scan.

sections.title: Date Format
bullets: For chart axis labels, use Mmm ’YY format (e.g., Feb ’24).

For all other dates, use DD Mmm YYYY format (e.g., 21 Mar 2024). To be discussed with users during design sprints and any deviation will have to be recorded in the respective service’s user story document.
Use leading zeros for single-digit days (e.g., 01 Jan 2024).

For month range pickers and input fields, write placeholder text as MM/YYYY but allow for multiple input formats (e.g., MM/YYYY, MM YYYY, MM YY, Mmm YYYY, Mmm YY). Once users click away or press the keyboard keys ‘Enter’/’Tab’, the fields will automatically be displayed as DD Mmm YYYY.
Use abbreviations for months (Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr, May, Jun, Jul, Aug, Sep, Oct, Nov, Dec).
Use abbreviations for days (Sun, Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat).
